translation: Thirty-two: The channels cross from the hands to the shoulders, reach behind the head, come out above the ears, descend the jaw to Quepen; the three yang channels, six roots on left and right, returning from Quepen to the neck and jaw, have already become twelve roots, eighteen in all, all encircling and attaching to the neck. Once silted and accumulated, the channels and vessels still flow, but the accumulation is silted and stops; accumulating again it becomes more, more again it becomes longer, longer again it becomes bent, and bent it hangs down as a double head, one root more. One root changes into three, becoming fifty-four roots; how could the neck not become thick? The nebula takes its supply from above; how could the scalp not become tight? From this the head also produces silted accumulation.
